title: Ultra-Thin LED Exterior Recessed Lighting Installation (Ask This Old House)

locations.name: Exterior doorway soffit area (probable)
locations.basis: Transcript references placing the light over a door and beneath a soffit; no explicit shooting location.

summary: The video demonstrates replacing an older, bulky recessed exterior light with a new ultra-thin LED recessed fixture. It explains the benefits of low-voltage operation (24V) derived from a 120V supply, and shows practical installation steps under a soffit, including mounting with clips and accommodating the soffit’s thickness. A key instructional focus is routing wiring to satisfy box capacity limits when adding multiple fixtures, followed by finishing with a digital astronomical wall switch to automate exterior lighting and a power-on reveal that highlights improved door illumination.

sections.title: Project framing: lighting options and driveway considerations
sections.description: Sets up the choice between floodlights for driveways and recessed/low-profile lighting near a doorway, noting glare issues with bright exterior lights and the aim for a cleaner door illumination.

sections.title: Old recessed fixture anatomy and soffit constraints
sections.description: Describes the existing recessed light: the trim, ~7 inches of housing, a hard bar, and the junction box, and discusses how soffit structure can complicate placement.

sections.title: Introduction of ultra-thin LED replacement & power architecture
sections.description: Introduces the replacement fixture as ultra-thin and LED-powered, with a 120V input and 24V output to the LED via a flexible cable.

sections.title: Installation approach: mounting, clips, and soffit fit
sections.description: Explains how the LED fixture is mounted using clips and is designed to fit in a 3/4 inch soffit, setting up for removal of the old fixture and installation of the new one.

sections.title: Wiring routing for two-box limit and multi-fixture feed
sections.description: Addresses the practical constraint of only two wires per junction box and describes routing the conductors to feed multiple fixtures from a single run.

sections.title: Automation and final reveal
sections.description: Concludes with powering the system back on and presenting the automated, door-illuminating effect enabled by a digital astronomical switch.
